1.08 There will be no new transmission facilities other than a probable line conversion from the Central Power and Light's existing facilities into the dam area and substation facilities. The conversion is considered a part of the onsite work to be completed during the construction period.
1.09 Construction Period. The construction period to add hydropower facilities to Amistad Dam has not been estimated in detail. A preliminary estimate is that about one or two years before onsite construction begins, a manufacturer will be engaged to design, model test, manufacture, and install the turbines, generators and certain appurtenant equipment. Actual onsite work should take about two to three years to complete. Only the onsite work should have any environmental consequences, and it is the point of reference when the construction period is discussed in this environmental statement.
1.10 Project Costs. The project cost is estimated to be about $28 million for hydroelectric power installation at Amistad Dam under the jurisdiction of the US Section IBWC (including engineering, plans, supervision, and administration).
1.11 Amistad-Falcon Systems Operation. The plan of operation includes operating the existing Falcon and the proposed Amistad hydroelectric plants as a two unit system. This proposed integrated systems operation is in accordance with the 1944 Water Treaty, IBWC Minutes, and Texas Water Rights Commission's (TWRC) regulatory procedures.
1.12 Studies indicate that the proposed operation of Amistad Reservoir will tend to slightly decrease the length of time that pool levels will be at or above specific elevations with the conservation pool. Conversely, conservation waters of Falcon Reservoir will experience a slight to moderate increase in the length of time that pool levels will be at or above specific elevations within the conservation pool. The net result of the proposed action will be to lower conservation water at Amistad Reservoir by an average of two feet while raising Falcon Reservoir about three feet.
1.13 Flood control releases from Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs will continue to be made by the IBWC at a minimum practicable rate, and if possible, at rates not exceeding the Rio Grande channel capacity. Under the proposed plan of operation, water supply releases from Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs through the turbines would continue to be under the regulating authority of the TWRC.
1.14 No reservoir capacity of Amistad and Falcon Reservoirs would be allocated to hydroelectric power, and there would be no minimum pool retained for power in either reservoir. No releases would be made from Amistad Reservoir for hydroelectric power which would result in spills from Falcon Reservoir, or in the transfer of ownership of water in Falcon Reservoir. Fluctuations in the day-to-day operation of the hydroelectric power plant at Amistad Dam cannot be forecast, but the daily release pattern is likely to be within the range of operations simulated in the April 1976 reservoir test releases. Reservoir operation studies of Falcon and Amistad Reservoirs, with and without hydroelectric power generation at Amistad Dam, were made on a monthly basis to serve the monthly water demands computed by the Texas Water Rights Commission. To be sure, within many months there will be large variations in daily irrigation demands due to rainfall on the Lower Rio Grande Valley, and conversely due to hot dry periods. These climatic fluctuations will result in significant changes in the daily irrigation releases from Falcon Reservoir.
